LocalAI on a Pentium 1! D:

Okay... not really. But I did compile and run an implementation of ELIZA on my Pentium 1 under NetBSD!

If you don't know ELIZA: it was one of the earliest chatbots, created by Joseph Weizenbaum at MIT in the 1960s. The best known version, DOCTOR, simulated a psychotherapist by recognizing keywords and responding with predefined patterns. It didn't actually understand what you were saying, but it could produce surprisingly convincing conversations and sometimes hilariously circular ones.

I actually know ELIZA from my school graduation thesis, which I wrote in psychology. So when I came across this C++ implementation, I couldn't resist bringing it back to life on my Pentium 1.

The original ELIZA was written for the IBM 7094 using MAD SLIP. My version is a modern C++ implementation of the ELIZA concept, not the original 1960s source code.

I even had a little conversation with it about... itself. Needless to say, ELIZA wasn't particularly interested in answering questions about ELIZA.

For the compilation, I used a NetBSD VM on my modern Linux machine with QEMU/KVM, configured with a Pentium CPU model, 128 MB RAM and a virtual NE2000 network card. I compiled the C++20 source inside that Pentium configured NetBSD environment and then transferred the resulting binary to the real Pentium 1.

So, no local LLM running on a 166 MHz Pentium 1... but a chatbot from the 1960s running on hardware from the 1990s feels almost perfectly appropriate D:
